probe: Live acceptance for issue #20, geometry leg (onshape_interference_check), run against the deployed Windows host on 2026-10-03. The tool itself was exercised end to end on the host; the last hop (the host's stored WSL distro name) is wrong and is reported here as a host-state defect rather than a code defect, because the same stored name breaks the pre-existing browser geometry backend too.
status: verified-through-the-real-launcher; the deployed run now names its own blocker; a fully deployed run waits on one host-state write that needs human approval
session: 2026-10-03, deployed host C:\MCP\onshapescript at 1.5.1 (generation 13) and 1.5.2 (generation 14), repo master c386853

verified.what: The deployed host assembles the exact intended argv and can read the STEP file.
verified.note: This is the 1.5.1 fallback at work on real host state: backend.owningMode=onshape_browser_mode, backend.fallback=true, because this mode's own config is disabled while the browser mode's is configured. The report is read from stdout, so the call writes nothing.

verified.what: The real Windows launcher runs the converter on that exact argv (distro name corrected) and produces the analytic answer.

overlap.analytic: two 10 mm boxes offset by (8, 7, 6) share a 2x3x4 mm region = 24.0 mm^3

interlock.analytic: an L-shaped part and the block that fills its notch overlap as boxes (3x3x10 mm) while sharing zero volume, which is exactly the false positive a bounding-box-only check cannot resolve

verified.note: The converter mapped the Windows path argument to /mnt/c/... by itself, so the same argv works whether the STEP path arrives as Windows or POSIX form.

verified.what: A failing backend can never be reported as a clean model.
verified.evidence: With the host's real (broken) config the deployed call returned verdict=indeterminate, failureClass=converter_failed, exitCode=4294967295, failures=['the interference converter exited 4294967295: '] at 1.5.1 -- a non-clean verdict with an empty reason. 1.5.2 fixes the empty reason by decoding the launcher's UTF-16 output and reporting a stdout tail.
verified.note: The verdict honesty held; the reason did not. That gap is the reason 1.5.2 exists.

verified.what: On the deployed host, 1.5.2 turns the empty reason into the launcher's own words.

host_state_defect.summary: The stored browser-mode geometry config names a WSL distribution that does not exist on this host, so every command assembled from it fails at the launcher.
measured: wsl.exe -l -v lists exactly one distribution: 'Ubuntu' (Running, WSL2, default)
host_state_defect.discovery_agrees: onshape_geometry_status on the host reports the WSL candidate da4a6b54820703d9b763 with distribution 'Ubuntu', i.e. live discovery knows the right name while the stored config keeps the wrong one.
host_state_defect.impact: Not specific to this feature: onshape_build_geometry_package and every other host-side user of the configured geometry backend fail the same way. browser.ready=true in that status is a CONFIG-level readiness and is not a probe that the command runs.
host_state_defect.sanctioned_repair: onshape_configure_geometry_backend(backend='rest', candidate_id='da4a6b54820703d9b763', confirm_mutation=true) after a dry_run preview. That writes only onshape_rest_api_mode/config/geometry-backend.json (operator state, never touched by an upgrade) and makes this mode's own config the primary for the interference check; the browser config is left alone.
host_state_defect.authority: A production configuration write needs the user's explicit approval, so it was NOT performed in this session. It is the only remaining step between the measured results above and a fully deployed live run.

how_to_finish: Get explicit approval for the sanctioned repair above (or accept the browser config's distro name being corrected by hand on the host).
Call onshape_interference_check(step_path='C:\\MCP\\onshapescript\\artifacts\\interference-acceptance\\overlap.step') and expect verdict=interference with intersection_volume_mm3 23.999999999999996.
Call the same for interlock.step and expect verdict=clean with zero_volume_contact true and interfering 0.
